evidence.claim: 3Q26 10-Q discloses for the first time that some TPU system contracts require Google to repurchase sold hardware at pre-set prices over a multi-year term: maximum potential payments $6.6bn; Google says the discount makes exercise uneconomic.
evidence.numbers: A residual-value floor on accelerators sold to customers; management called servers 6-year assets on the call. Inventory, mostly TPU systems, rose to $13.3bn from $2.4bn at year-end.

evidence.claim: SemiAnalysis reads Anthropic's revenue-per-megawatt jump partly as hardware: Blackwell is about 50x Hopper on their efficiency measure. Anthropic runs TPU, Trainium, Nvidia and AMD at once and says the software determines who gets the most from new chips. A 50x generational step is what a Hopper fleet's re-rent value is up against.
evidence.source: SemiAnalysis on Anthropic's S-1, 27 Oct 2026 (not yet checked against the filing)

evidence.claim: Meta still depreciates most servers over 5.5 years (unchanged since Jan 2025). Server depreciation is accelerating, and a large construction-in-progress balance is not yet depreciating. No analyst has asked about useful lives.
evidence.numbers: Servers/network depreciation $5.34bn in 3Q26 vs $3.60bn in 3Q25; CIP $89.50bn vs $50.52bn at YE25.

evidence.claim: Crusoe's CEO says older A100 and H100 chips rent for more now than when first deployed; Nebius says price per MW keeps rising.
evidence.numbers: Management statements without rate data (CNBC via Slicast).

evidence.claim: CFO says new compute at current prices pays back in under a year; Measured AI calculates about $44 per watt per year across five contracts, about $33 for Anthropic and near $50 for Google.
evidence.numbers: Measured AI estimates 10 to 12 months payback on operating cash, so Musk's six-month 2027 target looks hard.

evidence.claim: Raised prices about 25% in July and signed an A100 contract into 2029, but renewals so far cover a small part of the fleet; adjusted EBITDA margin 58.6% against operating margin 5.0% shows how much depreciation weighs.
Amin Vahdat says seven- and eight-year-old TPUs still run at full utilization; pods are replaced after about six years.
Its newest loan runs five years against three-year contracts, so lenders now carry the re-renting risk in years 4–5.
Lochmiller says H100 rental prices are now above where they were at launch three years ago; Crusoe depreciates over six years.

question: What do GPUs earn once their first contract ends, and does that justify six-year depreciation?
summary: Older chips are still holding value on management's telling: Crusoe says A100 and H100 rents exceed launch levels, and SpaceX says new compute pays back in under a year. But these are statements, not renewal data, and only a small part of fleets has come up for renewal; the test comes when 2027-28 supply is online and the first big block of contracts rolls off. Status unchanged.
title: What chips earn after their first contract
